payload.title: Definitions are applied by the release
payload.description:
The release registers each definition in the site's backend, as procedures are to be registered on deploy (PPY-1b2edd): an unchanged digest changes nothing; a changed one writes a new registered version; a definition removed from Git is marked retired, its schedule is removed and its history stays. The apply step never touches the agent policy document, so a deploy cannot change a rung or lift a pause. A new agent arrives at rung `off` unless the site's policy already names it.

**Acceptance criteria**
- A release with no definition change writes nothing.
- A new definition appears at `off` on a site that has no policy line for it.
- A deploy never changes a rung, a pause or a budget.
- Every behaviour change ships with narrative Gherkin specs (below).

**Gherkin features needed**
- agent-definitions-on-release.feature: an unchanged definition is a no-op; a changed one becomes a new version; a removed one is retired and its schedule deleted; a new agent starts `off`; the policy document is untouched.

**Infrastructure as code touched:** Site deploy step (the same place procedures are registered).

**Part of:** Agent definitions, the catalog and generated runbooks. Slice code D2 in `docs/design/always-on-agents-architecture.md` (section 12).
**Standing rules:** no fallbacks, no workarounds, no interim systems, no arbitrary caps; no text in DynamoDB; indexes over scans; no AppSync subscriptions; nothing created by hand in AWS; no real email addresses in specs or fixtures; status shown as words and marks, never colour alone.
